newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi leaders call for dialogue to mark Eid.
newsitem.headline: Saudi leaders call for dialogue to mark Eid.

text.p: Saudi Arabia's King Fahd and Crown Prince Abdullah marked the Islamic Eid al-Fitr feast by expressing their concern over bloodshed in Moslem countries, Saudi newspapers reported on Saturday.
"We are concerned by what is happening in some Moslem countries, the bloodshed and killing," the Saudi leaders said in a statement late on Friday, the newspapers said.
They called on Moslems to resort to dialogue to solve their disputes.
The Saudi leaders did not name any country but fighting has erupted early last month in Sudan between government forces and Sudanese rebels in the south and east of the country.
In Algeria, more than 300 people have been killed in political violence between Moslem fundamentalists and the authorities during the Moslem fasting month of Ramadan.
Saudi Arabia has also been hit by political violence.

The authorities are still investigating the June truck bombing of a military housing complex in Dhahran that killed 19 U.S. troops. Five other Americans died in a bombing at a Saudi National Guard facility in Riyadh in late 1995.
The Eid al-Fitr holiday marking the end of the fasting month of Ramadan lasts five days in Saudi Arabia and three days in other countries.
The official Saudi Press Agency (SPA) said King Fahd and other senior officials performed dawn prayers on Saturday in the holy city of Mecca along with other worshippers.
